title: AICompanionEngine Rule Configuration
description: Formal JSON Schema for AICompanionEngine rule JSON. Single source of truth for rule creation, validation, and form generation. The engine and contract versions this copy belongs to are in contract/versions.json; the distributable copy also carries them as x-engineVersion / x-schemaVersion. See JSON_RULE_STRUCTURE.md for full documentation.

rulesArray.description: Legacy document shape: a bare array of rules.

rulesEnvelope.description: Envelope document shape: an optional topics registry plus the rules array.

schemaVersion.description: The rule contract version this document was authored against, as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Absent means the 1.0.0 baseline. The engine rejects a document outside the range in contract/versions.json (supportedSchema.min..max).

_meta.description: Authoring metadata written by the rule builder; the engine ignores it.

topics.description: Registry of topic configurations, keyed by topic name. Names are normalized by the engine (trim, lowercase, whitespace to underscore).

precedence.description: Batch ordering rank. Outranks rule priority: priority only orders rules within equal precedence.

tone.description: Default tone for rules in this topic whose output declares no tone. A rule's own tone wins.

maxPerBatch.description: Maximum prompts from this topic in one concatenated batch. Overflow is announced in the composed prompt.

throttle.description: Topic-level budget shared across every rule carrying this topic. A rule held back by it keeps its own daily allowance.

rule.description: A single rule definition. Must have either 'output' or 'actions' (or both).

id.description: Unique rule identifier. The 'topic:' prefix is reserved for the engine's topic budget persistence.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the rule does.

actions.description: Top-level mobile app commands executed when rule fires.

topic.description: Theme grouping key (e.g. 'safety', 'adherence'). Normalized to a slug by the engine. Drives batch grouping/ordering, topic budgets, tone defaults and runtime muting. Should name an entry in the document's topics registry when one exists.

conversation.description: Whether a trigger of this rule is meant to open a conversation on its own. 'auto' (default) is the existing behaviour. 'manual' marks a rule the app should record without speaking - badges, counters, rollups - so normally no conversation happens for it at all. Advisory only: the engine delivers every triggered rule either way.

requiredVariables.description: Output variable ids that must resolve before this rule may fire. Holds the rule back rather than letting it fire with an incomplete prompt and burn its daily allowance. Every name must be declared in output.variables, or the rule can never fire.

sessionScope.description: Session lifetime. global = app lifetime, daily = 24h reset, activity = until endActivityScope() (an activity is a trip in the fleet app, high intent action in other products ect.). Case-insensitive in engine.

cooldownMinutes.description: Minutes to wait between triggers. 0 = can fire again immediately.

maxTriggersPerDay.description: Maximum times this rule can fire per day. Resets at day boundary.

triggerExpression.description: What events must occur for the rule to fire. Either a SINGLE event or a GROUP of expressions.

singleTrigger.description: Matches one specific event from one data source.

id.description: Event name (non-API sources) or trigger ID (API sources). Must be a predefined value — see JSON_RULE_STRUCTURE.md.

conditions.description: Filter conditions. All conditions use AND logic.

extractedParameters.description: Parameter names to extract from matched events.

dateRangeInDays.description: Time period for API data retrieval, set on the SINGLE trigger expression (not on the variable). Default 1. Applies to DRIVER_MEASUREMENTS_SCORE, TRIP_EVENTS, TRIP_DETAILS, THERAPY_SESSIONS and PATIENT_EXERCISES. The window runs backwards from now for every type except PATIENT_EXERCISES, where it runs forwards - dateRangeInDays 1 on patient_exercises means the next 24 hours.

allOf.description: Wellness triggers: restrict condition parameters and extractable keys to the fields actually emitted in wellness_measurement_taken attrs (see WellnessRepositoryImpl in FleetDrive-Android).

groupTrigger.description: Combines multiple trigger expressions with AND/OR logic. Can be nested.

groupType.description: AND = all must match, OR = at least one matches.

expressions.description: Array of SINGLE or nested GROUP expressions.

dataSource.description: Event origin. API sources: MZONE, GZONE, External Source, MojoPortal. Although the engine matches data sources case-insensitively, the event-buffer lookup and date-range extraction compare the literal string, so a rule must use the exact casing listed here - 'mojoportal' matches but then silently finds no events. Mojo = on-device events from the Mojo app; MojoPortal = the Mojo portal REST API, which never emits events itself and must be paired with a triggering event in an AND group.

condition.description: Filter condition on a trigger expression. Discriminated by 'type' field.

valueCondition.description: Compares an event parameter against a value.

parameter.description: Event parameter name to compare (e.g. 'speed', 'hour', 'poi_type'). The unit of `value` is whatever the source emits — the engine compares raw numbers and never converts. SmartDrive: `speed` km/h, `duration` seconds, `distance` WHOLE KILOMETRES (truncated to an integer, so anything under 1 km arrives as 0), `duration_millis` milliseconds. MHub: `distance` metres, `duration` and `stationary_time` seconds, `speed`/`max_speed` km/h, `brake_force`/`acceleration_force` whole km/h/s (not g), `rpm`/`max_rpm` rpm in steps of 100, `fuel_level` %, temperatures °C, `voltage` V. POI `radius` metres. Note SmartDrive and MHub disagree on `distance` — km vs metres. Mixing these up is silent: the condition just stays false. See JSON_RULE_STRUCTURE.md → Parameters by Data Source.

value.description: Comparison value, in the unit the parameter is emitted in — see `parameter`. A single value for every operator except 'in', which takes an array. Type it as the parameter is emitted: `program_week` arrives as the JSON number 4, so write 4 and [4, 8, 12], not "4" and ["4", "8", "12"]. The engine matches a quoted number against a numeric parameter anyway, but the validator warns, because a quoted numeral is otherwise indistinguishable from a genuine string identifier.

source.description: Optional source identifier for filtering (e.g. 'MHUB', 'Beacon' for BLE).

eventName.description: Optional event selector. Present, the lookup becomes an exact (dataSource, eventName) match instead of a search for any event carrying `parameter`. Use it when several events under one data source share a parameter name.

wellnessValueCondition.description: Stricter valueCondition for Wellness triggers. `parameter` is restricted to the 9 keys actually emitted in wellness_measurement_taken attrs. `wellnessLevel` values are constrained to the Wellness framework WellnessLevel enum. Numeric-typed parameters require numeric values.

value.description: Comparison value. Narrowed per-parameter by the allOf rules below.

eventName.description: Optional event selector; see valueCondition.eventName. Wellness emits a single event name today, so this is rarely needed here.

allOf.description: wellnessLevel must match the Wellness framework enum (UNKNOWN / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH).

Numeric wellness fields (int / double) require a numeric value, including inside an 'in' set. This branch used to exempt `in` and accept a string array, which the engine then compared element-by-element against a JSON number and never matched.

conditionScalar.description: A single comparison value. Typed as the parameter is emitted — a numeric parameter takes a number, a string parameter a string, a flag a boolean.

conditionValue.description: What a Value condition compares against: one scalar, or — for 'in' — a set of them. The item type mirrors the parameter's own type, so a numeric parameter takes [4, 8, 12] and a string parameter ["MON", "TUE"]. A set that mixes types cannot match on every element and is warned about.

operatorValueShape.description: Couples `value`'s shape to the operator reading it. Both mistakes this rejects used to validate and then fail silently at runtime: 'in' against a scalar has no set to search, and a scalar operator handed an array cannot compare against it.

timeRangeCondition.description: Checks if current UTC time falls within a range. Handles midnight crossing automatically.

from.description: Start time in HH:MM 24-hour UTC format.

to.description: End time in HH:MM 24-hour UTC format.

timeCondition.description: Compares the current UTC time against a single value. No event in buffer required.

comparisonCondition.description: Compares values across two time periods (e.g. this month vs last month). Requires 'parameter' or 'leaderboardId' (or both).

leaderboardId.description: Leaderboard ID. Required if parameter is absent.

value.description: Threshold for the difference between periods.

eventCountCondition.description: Counts occurrences of a specific event in the current session.

aggregateCondition.description: Reduces a numeric field across every matching event in a rolling time window (min/max/avg/sum/count) and compares the result against a threshold.

op.description: Reducer applied to the window. 'count' counts events and ignores 'field'; every other op requires 'field'.

field.description: Numeric event attribute to reduce (e.g. 'average_rom'). Required unless op is 'count'.

value.description: Threshold the reduced value is compared against.

window.description: Rolling window looking back from now: '7d', '12h', '30m'.

scope.description: Session whose history is read. Omit to read the rule's own session. Only 'global' can be named - daily and activity session ids embed a date or activity id.

relativeTimeWindowCondition.description: Checks if a timestamp parameter falls within a time window from now.

fromNow.description: Time offset. '1h' = within 1h future, '-4h' = within 4h past, '30m' = 30min, '-2d' = 2 days ago.

aggregateOperator.description: Comparison operator for Aggregate conditions. An aggregate reduces to a number, so 'in' and 'contains' do not apply.

operator.description: Comparison operator. 'in' takes a set — an array whose items are typed as the parameter is emitted, so [4, 8, 12] for a numeric parameter and ["MON", "TUE"] for a string one. Every other operator takes a single value. 'contains' does a case-insensitive substring match on string values (e.g. "circle" matches "Circle K"); for list-valued fields it matches if any element contains the substring.

poi.description: Point of Interest configuration for location-based triggers.

output.description: LLM prompt configuration. The engine constructs: instructions + tone + resolved variables + wellness auto-context.

instructions.description: What to tell the LLM. Reference data naturally — variables are appended automatically.

variables.description: Data to extract and include in the LLM prompt.

actions.description: Actions embedded in output (combined with LLM prompt).

variable.description: Defines what data to extract from events/APIs and include in the LLM prompt.

id.description: Variable identifier used as key in prompt. Special IDs: 'firstname', 'get_todays_jobs', 'fuel_range', 'current_location', 'job_details'.

source.description: JSON key of array/object in API response (e.g. 'jobs', 'value', '_rawJobs').

fields.description: Specific fields to extract from each object (uses FieldExtractor).

triggerId.description: Links variable to a specific trigger expression ID. Disambiguates multiple API calls to same dataSource.

filters.description: Filter conditions (AND logic) applied to array elements before extraction.

value.description: Accepted but not read by this engine - RuleVariable has no such field, so writing it changes nothing. Name the parameter in 'id' instead. It stays in the grammar so documents already carrying it remain valid, and the validator warns when it appears.

followUp.description: A conversation-specific yes/no question asked after the rule triggers. The normalized answer is emitted to mobile; no action payload is configured here.

id.description: Stable identifier unique within this rule.

action.description: Mobile app command. Known types: SetReminder, APICall, PhoneCall, OpenScreen. All extra fields are passed as parameters to mobile.
